text:
jess (Support): @oliver heads-up — customer nora@acme-eu reporting large p99 (2-3s) and some 503s since 08:30 UTC. They’re on a dedicated EU reservation but traces show requests routed to hosted-us-east. Billing shows hosted token charges. Investigating.

oliver (Oncall Eng): thanks jess. do we have a repro? can nora share a request id or sample ts?

nora (Customer): hi — sample request id 01F8ZQH2Q0F8X4C0M1 (08:34:12 UTC). we noticed it right after some autoscale events. app logs show timeouts, then a bunch of 502/503s. happy to keep a session live for testing.

jess (Support): repro steps I used:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REPRO_TOKEN" -H "X-Org: acme-eu" -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt": "test"}'
```
response: 200 served from hosted-us-east, latency 2.8s.

maya (Runtime): initial hypothesis: affinity table TTL drifted during the autoscale/backfill window; router looked at stale pin and fell back to hosted pool. can you dump the affinity key for that tenant?

liam (SRE): i pulled redis keys for tenant:acme-eu at 08:33:50 UTC:
```
key: pin:tenant:acme-eu -> {"pool":"eu-dedicated-A","expires_at":1718202000}
```
then at 08:34:05 UTC it flips to null / not found and router chooses hosted fallback. looks like TTL expired earlier than expected.

oliver (Oncall Eng): where is TTL normally refreshed? is it the assigner / dedicated-agent heartbeat or router's read-when-binding flow?\
maya (Runtime): TTL should be refreshed by the dedicated-agent on each allocation heartbeat. but i see recent change in assignment code that updates only when load>0; in low-burst periods the heartbeat skipped refresh and TTL went negative during the autoscale shrink.

jess (Support): customer reports they were mid-session, so skipping refresh on low load is bad. also billing side: they got charged on hosted because fallback path accepted tokens.

liam (SRE): related auth glitch: some hosted endpoints accept tokens without region scoping and mark them hosted-billed. i see 401s earlier too:
```
2024-06-12T08:33:59Z auth: tenant=acme-eu token=... validation=ok region_hint=eu but route=hosted-us-east
```
not blocked, so request flows through hosted pool.

oliver (Oncall Eng): steps: 1) temporarily pin them back to eu-dedicated (force-bind) and restart the dedicated-agent to force TTL refresh. 2) patch router to prefer sticky-binding if token region==tenant region until TTL fix. 3) longer-term: change heartbeat logic to refresh TTL even at load=0.

jess (Support): actioning step 1 now — forcing bind to eu-dedicated-A for tenant acme-eu. will monitor metrics. @deploy-bot can you note that we forced bind for tenant acme-eu?

deploy-bot: Action recorded — forced-binding tenant=acme-eu -> pool=eu-dedicated-A by jess at 2024-06-12T08:45:12Z.

nora (Customer): confirming — after the forced bind we see p99 back to ~120ms, no 503s. thanks.

maya (Runtime): opened PR to always refresh TTL on heartbeat even if no active requests: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/542 (tests included). putting this in tomorrow's hotfix.

liam (SRE): created monitoring alert to detect TTL drift events (count of pin keys with expires_at < now but recently assigned) and a billing audit to flag hosted charges for tenants with active dedicated reservations. ticket #INC-4521.

oliver (Oncall Eng): nice. can we also add a temporary router rule: if token region header==tenant.region and tenant has active reservation -> prefer dedicated route (even if fallback exists). small guard to reduce customer impact while we patch.

jess (Support): agreed. i've told nora we'll follow up when the hotfix deploys. i'll keep this thread updated. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

nora (Customer): appreciated — please CC me on INC-4521 so we can reconcile billing.

jess (Support): will do, tagging finance & billing after SRE posts audit.

oliver (Oncall Eng): assigning ownership: runtime/maya -> hotfix PR, sRE/liam -> billing audit and alert, support/jess -> customer comms. closing loop after hotfix verification.

maya (Runtime): ETA for hotfix deploy to canary: 2024-06-12T15:00Z. I'll post results here.

jess (Support): marking resolved for now since bind restored service — will reopen if recurrence.
